objective: Close the four structurally echo-less lever classes found by the dead-lever audit: every load-bearing solver lever must either print its own runtime banner (sub-LU style) or be echoed into the run log by the launcher at t=0, so charter v1.5 section 9 levers_verified_active is satisfiable at write time instead of failing retroactively
rationale: The 2026-08-08 dead-lever audit (campaign/DEAD_LEVER_AUDIT_2026-08-08.md, 946e4a26) verified 126 lever-conclusion pairs from runtime logs and found that every one of its 16 unverifiable-from-logs entries traces to four lever classes that stock OpenFOAM structurally never echoes: (1) fvSchemes tokens -- no scheme selection is ever printed on success, which is why the TMR NACA 0012 scheme-substitution root cause, the A3 Stage-2 shock-scheme claim, and six DEFECT_ROBUSTNESS scheme arms rest on field-delta inference instead of an echo; (2) fvSolution 'consistent yes' (SIMPLEC) -- simpleFoam prints identical 'SIMPLE:' banners either way, which is why the F5c -10.5% headline's algorithm attribution and the Ahmed A4 baseline half are unverifiable forever from existing logs; (3) boundary-condition types -- never echoed at runtime, distinguishable only through outcome shifts (the freestreamVelocity-vs-inletOutlet arms' CD0 discriminator); (4) dictionary values with no printout -- mu in thermophysicalProperties, MRF omega magnitude/sign. The positive template already exists in the lab twice over: the DALinearEqn sub-LU patch prints 'DAFOAM_SUBPC_TYPE=lu: ASM sub-block PC set to complete LU' at activation, the archive holds a negative control proving the off-state (cbfs_regress log: no banner, reason -9), and every conclusion-bearing sub-LU run asserts the banner before trusting the result; DAFoam's daOptions dump and OpenFOAM's turbulence-model printCoeffs are the same pattern natively. Proposed mechanics, report-only, for Infra to adopt with their own verification: (a) the common launch wrappers (scripts/launch_solve.sh and the sdk workflow builders that assemble cases) cat system/fvSchemes, system/fvSolution, constant/MRFProperties, constant/thermophysicalProperties and the 0/ BC files into the run log before invoking the solver, delimited with a LEVER-ECHO header and the case path plus a sha256 of each file so the echo is bound to the artifact that ran; (b) any lab-built patch that adds a lever must print an activation banner AND leave a distinguishable off-state (the sub-LU B-1 hazard -- unrecognized env values silently fall back to stock with no tell -- is what the banner-assert discipline exists to catch; new patches should hard-fail on unrecognized values instead of falling through); (c) the record-writing convention gains the assertion pattern: a levers_verified_active entry cites either the code's own banner line or the launcher's LEVER-ECHO block line, and a pre-registration naming a lever from classes 1-4 is rejected at filing unless the plan's launcher does the echo. Cost is zero solver time; the alternative is what the audit measured -- 16 conclusions that must carry unverifiable-from-logs on their face because the evidence was structurally impossible to have kept.
cost_basis: measured; the audit that produced the class inventory is already spent, the mechanics are launcher/wrapper code changes with no solver time
expected_knowledge_gain: The four lever classes that today can only be verified by field-delta inference or not at all become log-provable at launch for every future run; levers_verified_active stops being retroactively unsatisfiable, and the F5c-class failure (a load-bearing algorithm attribution with no possible surviving evidence) becomes unreachable
